AUTHOR: Marjadi
TITLE: A video monitoring and computational system for estimating migratory juvenile fish abundance in river systems
REGION: Monument (Herring) River fish ladder exit, Bourne, Massachusetts, USA
SPECIES: Juvenile river herring (Alosa pseudoharengus and A. aestivalis, not distinguished)
DATA: Own continuous monochrome/IR video, June-Nov 2017 (8 training videos, 10 evaluation videos; Zooniverse-labelled evaluation set)
V_EV: Testing performance across conditions / Table 5: 'Model performance for presence/absence of juvenile river herring across filming conditions: month, time of day, cloud cover, and moon phase'; Fig. 3 'different turbidity'.
D2: Training dataset (8 videos) split 89/10/1 frames; final evaluation on 10 separate videos (19,498 frames) plus 188-frame count set
D_EV: Model evaluation dataset selection: 'To evaluate model performance on new data, we processed a second set of videos (10), which spanned a range of conditions and time periods.'
R_EV: Video specifications: single camera at 'the exit of the furthest downstream fish ladder in the Monument River' June-Nov 2017; training and evaluation videos both from this deployment.
C_EV: Evaluation dataset: 'we used a random image selector to extract 11,395 model-identified positive frames ... to be marked on Zooniverse'; frame extraction 'To avoid overcounting fish present in multiple video frames'.
E_EV: Numerical count performance: 'the count evaluation dataset reported 3339 fish in 189 images, while the top model counted 3686 fish'; Fig. 5 daily estimated juvenile emigration numbers.
ARCH: YOLOv5 (detector/counter, selected); ResNet101 and Inception v3 categorical count classifiers; optional motion-encoding preprocessing
METR: Precision, recall, F1 (presence/absence and categorical), per-frame count difference, % count difference, Pearson r
NOTE: Headline evaluation on 10 videos separate from the 8 training videos (same site, same 2017 season) -> D1=video, R1=N. No detection confidence threshold reported. C5: model-identified positive/negative frames sampled and verified by Zooniverse volunteers/experts (FP counted), and frame-residence-rate frame extraction to avoid double counting. E1 '복수': comparison with human counts of same footage plus daily abundance/passage time series (Fig. 5). Assessment data in a data release (Marjadi et al. 2023); code on GitHub. TAXA: two Alosa species treated as one class.
AUTHORS_FULL: Marjadi, MN; Batchelder, S; Govostes, R; Roy, AH; Sheppard, JJ; Slocombe, MG; Llopiz, JK
